ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Counterparty Paper Review
Matter File 6 — Contracts Work

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
Prepared for Client | Partner Review

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES ON THE REDLINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This redline reflects the counterparty's latest paper as marked against the base 
Account Control Agreement and the firm's internal playbook (Account Control 
Agreement – Playbook v2.3), reconciled against the executed credit agreement, 
the depository bank's standard form, account details, and deal correspondence. 

Conventions:
- [Deletion] = text struck from counterparty draft / base standard form
- [INSERTION] = text added to conform to playbook and base agreement
- Each change cross-references the corresponding issue in the issues/risk memo.

Partner instruction (controlling, per deal correspondence): The client will 
concede the basket conversion (deductible-to-tipping). Any survival-period 
reduction is a walk-away issue and MUST be rejected without counter.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 "Account" means [the deposit account identified in Schedule A / the deposit 
account bearing account number [____] maintained with the Depository Bank in 
the name of the Debtor.]

1.2 "Account Control Agreement" means this Agreement, as amended, restated, 
supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time.

1.3 "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on [the business, 
condition (financial or otherwise), assets or operations of the Debtor] taken 
as a whole, OTHER THAN, IN EACH CASE, ANY EFFECT RESULTING FROM: (a) changes in 
general economic, political, financial or market conditions; (b) changes in 
laws, rules, regulations or GAAP; (c) any action taken in accordance with this 
Agreement; or (d) [DELETION: any action or inaction by any Governmental 
Authority, INCLUDING ANY REGULATORY INVESTIGATION, INQUIRY, PROCEEDING OR 
ENFORCEMENT ACTION RELATED TO THE ACCOUNT OR THE COLLATERAL — INSERTION: to the 
extent not caused by the Debtor's breach of its representations or covenants 
under the Credit Agreement] — SEE ISSUE 2.

1.4 "Basket" means [the threshold described in Section 6.3 / the deductible 
amount set forth in Section 6.3] CONVERTED TO A TIPPING BASKET — SEE ISSUE 1 
(CONCEDED BY CLIENT).

1.5 "Survival Period" means, with respect to any representation or warranty, 
the period during which such representation or warranty shall survive as set 
forth in Exhibit B. [DELETION: THE SURVIVAL PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS 
SHALL BE REDUCED TO 12 MONTHS — REJECTED — SEE ISSUE 3.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.7 Regulatory Compliance. The Debtor represents and warrants that, except as 
set forth on Schedule 3.7 (which discloses [TWO PENDING REGULATORY INQUIRIES 
CONCERNING [DESCRIBE] AND [DESCRIBE]]), the Debtor is in compliance with all 
applicable laws, rules and regulations.

REDLINE NOTE: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The 
counterparty's proposed MAE carve-out at Section 1.3(d) would exclude from 
"Material Adverse Effect" precisely this category of regulatory action. Reject 
the carve-out; reference the Schedule 3.7 disclosures for transparency without 
altering the MAE definition. — SEE ISSUE 2.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 5 — COVENANTS / RETAINED LIABILITIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.2 Retained Liabilities. The Debtor shall remain solely responsible for all 
retained liabilities set forth on Schedule 5.2. [DELETION: THE INDEMNIFICATION 
CAP FOR RETAINED LIABILITIES IS REDUCED FROM [AMOUNT] TO [THRESHOLD] — REJECTED 
— SEE ISSUE 1.] Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain fully indemnifiable 
without reduction by the cap.

REDLINE NOTE: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that would be silently 
shifted by the counterparty's indemnification changes. Restoration of the 
playbook cap and full indemnification of Schedule 5.2 liabilities is required. 
— SEE ISSUE 1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 6 — INDEMNIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 The Debtor shall indemnify and hold harmless the Secured Party and its 
affiliates from and against all losses, claims, damages, liabilities and 
related expenses arising out of any breach of representation, warranty, 
covenant or obligation under this Agreement.

6.3 Indemnification Limit. The aggregate liability of the Debtor under this 
Agreement shall not exceed [DELETION: THE REDUCED CAP OF [THRESHOLD] — 
INSERTION: THE CAP SET FORTH IN THE PLAYBOOK AT [AMOUNT] AND MATCHING THE 
EXECUTED CREDIT AGREEMENT]. The basket shall be a [CONVERTED TIPPING BASKET 
(CONCEDED BY CLIENT) — former deductible structure deleted]. — SEE ISSUE 1.

REDLINE NOTE: The counterparty silently reduced the indemnification cap. 
Restore the playbook/credit agreement cap. The basket conversion from 
deductible to tipping is conceded per partner instruction; however, the 
reduced cap is NOT conceded and must be restored. — SEE ISSUE 1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 9 — TERMINATION AND SURVIVAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.2 Survival. This Agreement and the representations, warranties and covenants 
contained herein shall survive termination as set forth in Exhibit B. 
[DELETION: NOTWITHSTANDING EXHIBIT B, THE CORE REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES 
SHALL SURVIVE THE CLOSING DATE FOR ONLY 12 MONTHS — REJECTED — WALK-AWAY ISSUE. 
INSERTION: THE SURVIVAL MATRIX SET FORTH IN EXHIBIT B SHALL GOVERN IN FULL.]

REDLINE NOTE: The counterparty's new limitation period shortens survival for 
core representations, directly contradicting Exhibit B's survival matrix. This 
is a walk-away issue per the controlling partner instruction. Reject without 
counter and require Exhibit B survival periods in full. — SEE ISSUE 3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXHIBIT B — SURVIVAL MATRIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[UNCHANGED — The Exhibit B survival matrix as executed in the credit agreement 
remains in full force. The counterparty's proposed 12-month reduced survival 
for core representations is rejected.]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END OF REDLINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
ISSUES/RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter File 6 — Contracts Work

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
Prepared for Client | Partner Review

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the counterparty's latest paper for the Account Control 
Agreement (the "ACA") against (i) the firm's internal playbook (Account Control 
Agreement – Playbook v2.3, the "Playbook"), (ii) the executed credit agreement 
(the "Credit Agreement"), (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) the 
account details set forth in the schedules, and (v) deal correspondence and 
closing checklists. The counterparty's markup accepts most firm-standard 
provisions but introduces three material deviations, each of which is analyzed 
below.

Controlling partner instruction (per the latest message in the deal 
correspondence, which supersedes all earlier messages): the client will 
concede the basket conversion, but any survival-period reduction is treated as 
a walk-away issue and must be rejected without counter.

Summary of findings:
1. Indemnification cap reduced and basket converted from deductible to 
   tipping — cap reduction REJECTED, basket conversion CONCEDED.
2. Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with carve-outs for 
   regulatory action of the exact kind at issue — REJECT.
3. New limitation period shortens survival for core representations — 
   REJECT; WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

None of the deviations is acceptable in its entirety. Two are subject to 
concession or revision; one is non-negotiable.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION BY DEVIATION ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEV 1: INDEMNIFICATION — CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION REFERENCES:
- ACA Section 6.1 (Indemnification obligation)
- ACA Section 6.3 (Indemnification Limit)
- ACA Section 5.2 (Retained Liabilities)
- Schedule 5.2 (Retained liabilities list)
- Playbook Section 4.2 (Indemnification and baskets)
- Credit Agreement Article X (Indemnification)

DESCRIPTION OF DEVIATION:
The counterparty's markup (i) silently reduces the aggregate indemnification 
cap from the amount set forth in the Playbook/executed Credit Agreement to a 
lower threshold, and (ii) converts the indemnification basket from a 
deductible to a tipping basket. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that 
would be silently shifted by these changes — the reduced cap would cap 
recovery on these liabilities below their aggregate value, and the basket 
conversion would shift the first-dollar loss to the Secured Party once the 
threshold is reached.

PLAYBOOK REQUIREMENT:
- Playbook section 4.2: The indemnification cap must match the cap set forth 
  in the executed Credit Agreement. No silent reduction is permitted without 
  express client approval.
- Playbook section 4.2(b): Basket structure (deductible vs. tipping) is 
  presumptively a deductible; any conversion requires explicit client 
  concession.
- Playbook section 4.2(c): Retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2 
  must be fully indemnifiable under the cap.

RISK RATING: MEDIUM-HIGH
The cap reduction creates a material financial exposure for the Secured Party 
by limiting recovery on breaches and claims, including the retained 
liabilities disclosed on Schedule 5.2. The basket conversion alone is a 
negotiating concession the client has decided to accept; the cap reduction 
results in an actual reduction of recoverable value.

EXPOSURE ANALYSIS:
- Cap reduction: If the cap is reduced from the base cap amount to the reduced 
  threshold, the Secured Party's recoverable exposure on Schedule 5.2 
  retained liabilities is reduced by the difference. A reduction on aggregate 
  claims above the reduced threshold would be recoverable by the Debtor's 
  limitation of liability.
- Basket conversion (deductible to tipping): Converts first-dollar risk to 
  the Secured Party once the threshold is exceeded, but only affects the 
  timing of recovery, not the ultimate amount. This is the conceded element.
- Schedule 5.2 interplay: The retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 are listed 
  to be fully indemnifiable. The cap reduction, if accepted, would silently 
  cap recovery on these liabilities, contradicting Schedule 5.2's purpose.

RECOMMENDED POSITION:
- REJECT the cap reduction. Restore the cap to the amount set forth in the 
  executed Credit Agreement and the Playbook.
- CONCEDE the basket conversion from deductible to tipping, per the 
  controlling partner instruction.
- Confirm Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain fully indemnifiable under 
  the restored cap.
- If the counterparty insists on the reduced cap, require an increase to the 
  negotiable range and obtain express client approval.

WALK-AWAY / DEAL-BREAKER STATUS: No, unless the counterparty refuses to restore 
the cap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEV 2: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — EXPANDED CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION REFERENCES:
- ACA Section 1.3 (Definition of "Material Adverse Effect")
- ACA Section 3.7 (Regulatory compliance representation)
- Schedule 3.7 (Disclosure of two pending regulatory inquiries)
- Playbook Section 2.1 (MAE definition requirements)
- Credit Agreement Section 1.01 (MAE definition)

DESCRIPTION OF DEVIATION:
The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the definition of "Material 
Adverse Effect" for regulatory action, specifically excluding from "material 
adverse effect" any action or inaction by any Governmental Authority, 
including any regulatory investigation, inquiry, proceeding or enforcement 
action related to the Account or the Collateral. This carve-out is of exactly 
the kind at issue in this matter: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending 
regulatory inquiries that relate to the Account and/or Collateral. The effect 
of the carve-out would be to remove the Debtor's obligation to represent and 
warrant compliance with respect to exactly the matters that are already known 
to be under investigation, thereby eliminating the Secured Party's recourse 
for those specific regulatory exposures.

PLAYBOOK REQUIREMENT:
- Playbook section 2.1: MAE carve-outs may not exclude matters that are (i) 
  already the subject of a disclosed pending regulatory inquiry, or (ii) 
  within the ordinary course of the Debtor's obligations under the Credit 
  Agreement. Carve-outs for Governmental Authority action may be acceptable 
  only where the action is not caused by the Debtor's own breach.
- Credit Agreement section 1.01: The MAE definition in the executed Credit 
  Agreement contains no regulatory-action carve-out of the type proposed.

RISK RATING: HIGH
This is a substantively material deviation. If accepted, the carve-out would 
eliminate the Secured Party's ability to assert a Material Adverse Effect (and 
therefore various related remedies) based on precisely the two regulatory 
inquiries already disclosed on Schedule 3.7. It is directionally inconsistent 
with the purpose of Schedule 3.7, which is to provide transparency regarding 
known regulatory exposure.

EXPOSURE ANALYSIS:
- The two pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7. If either inquiry 
  results in an adverse determination, a material adverse effect could 
  plausibly arise.
- Under the proposed carve-out, the Debtor could argue that no Material 
  Adverse Effect exists (or that the MAE exception to conditions precedent 
  does not apply) because the regulatory action falls within the excluded 
  Governmental Authority action carve-out.
- Result: The Secured Party would lose its ability to decline to fund, 
  accelerate, or exercise other MAE-based remedies with respect to the exact 
  exposures most likely to materialize.

RECOMMENDED POSITION:
- REJECT the carve-out in its entirety. 
- If concession is required as a negotiating matter, narrow the carve-out to 
  exclude only regulatory actions not caused by the Debtor's breach and that 
  arise from actions taken by a Governmental Authority without any Debtor 
  contribution. Even this narrower carve-out must explicitly exclude the 
  matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
- Reference Schedule 3.7 disclosures to ensure transparency without 
  structurally altering the MAE analysis.
- Confirm the MAE definition matches the Credit Agreement section 1.01.

WALK-AWAY / DEAL-BREAKER STATUS: Not per se, but a material issue requiring 
strong pushback.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEV 3: SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION REFERENCES:
- ACA Section 9.2 (Termination and Survival)
- Exhibit B (Survival matrix)
- Playbook Section 6.3 (Survival provisions)
- Credit Agreement Section 10.01 (Survival)

DESCRIPTION OF DEVIATION:
The counterparty's markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the 
survival of the core representations and warranties from the periods set forth 
in Exhibit B (the survival matrix) to a reduced period of 12 months. This 
directly contradicts Exhibit B, which sets specific, longer survival periods 
for core representations (including, among others, the regulatory compliance 
representation at Section 3.7 and the retained liabilities representation at 
Section 5.2).

PLAYBOOK REQUIREMENT:
- Playbook section 6.3: Survival periods for core representations must mirror 
  those set forth in the executed Credit Agreement and Exhibit B. No 
  unilateral reduction is permitted without express client approval. Core 
  representations include representations relating to regulatory compliance 
  and retained liabilities.
- Credit Agreement section 10.01: The credit agreement sets survival for core 
  representations for the full statute of limitations (or such other period 
  as set forth in Exhibit B).
- Exhibit B: Sets the governing survival matrix. The counterparty's change 
  contradicts this exhibit.

RISK RATING: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY
Per the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a 
walk-away issue. The counterparty's markup directly proposes such a reduction. 
This is non-negotiable.

EXPOSURE ANALYSIS:
- A shortened survival period would bar the Secured Party from asserting 
  claims for breaches of core representations (including the regulatory 
  compliance and retained liability representations) after the reduced period.
- Given the pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7 and the retained 
  liabilities on Schedule 5.2, a 12-month survival window would likely expire 
  before investigation outcomes or liability determination become known, 
  effectively extinguishing the Secured Party's recourse.
- The direct contradiction with Exhibit B creates ambiguity risk even if the 
  change were otherwise acceptable.

RECOMMENDED POSITION:
- REJECT the survival-period reduction without counteroffer.
- Require that the survival provisions remain unchanged from Exhibit B and 
  the Credit Agreement section 10.01.
- Flag to the partner that this is a walk-away issue per the controlling 
  instruction, and that no negotiation position should be offered.
- If the counterparty refuses to withdraw, recommend escalating to the client 
  for walk-away consideration.

WALK-AWAY / DEAL-BREAKER STATUS: YES — WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. MISSING PROTECTIONS AND OFF-MARKET TERMS IDENTIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In addition to the three counterparty deviations analyzed above, the following 
missing protections and off-market terms should be noted:

A. MISSING: Section 3.7 regulatory compliance representation does not include 
   an express covenant to update Schedule 3.7 disclosures in advance of 
   closing. Recommendation: add a bring-down covenant requiring the Debtor to 
   supplement Schedule 3.7 at closing and when any new regulatory inquiry is 
   commenced. — See Note A.

B. OFF-MARKET: The counterparty markup does not address the interplay between 
   the ACA and the executed Credit Agreement's automatic stay provisions. Best 
   practice under the Playbook requires an express acknowledgment that the 
   ACA's rights are subject to the Credit Agreement's remedies framework, 
   including acceleration. Recommend adding a conforming cross-reference. — 
   See Note B.

C. MISSING: The counterparty markup omits the standard "certificate of 
   control" delivery obligation set forth in the Playbook section 5.4. The 
   executed Credit Agreement requires the depository bank to deliver a 
   certificate of control upon request. Restore this obligation. — See Note C.

D. OFF-MARKET: The counterparty's markup does not include a provision 
   addressing termination of the ACA upon payment in full of the obligations 
   under the Credit Agreement. The Playbook section 7.1 requires an automatic 
   termination provision. Recommend adding. — See Note D.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#1 — Indemnification Cap & Basket (Section 6.3)
Counterparty Markup: Cap reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping
Playbook Requirement: Cap = credit agreement cap; basket presumptively deductible
Risk Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH
